rationale: The literature consistently demonstrates that mitochondrial iron-sulfur (Fe-S) cluster biogenesis and lipoylation defects (including NFU1, GLRX5, BOLA3, IBA57, and LIAS) share a convergent clinical and biochemical presentation. Specifically, both NFU1-related spastic paraplegia (SPG93) and GLRX5- or BOLA3-related disorders present as variant non-ketotic hyperglycinemia with elevated plasma/CSF glycine, deficient lipoylation of mitochondrial enzyme complexes, spastic paraparesis, peripheral neuropathy, and leukodystrophy or spinal cord signal abnormalities. No identified studies demonstrate clinical or biochemical pathognomonic features that reliably separate SPG93 from other Fe-S cluster lipoylation defects on phenotype alone, establishing that molecular genetic analysis is essential for definitive diagnosis.

evidence.text: Lipoic acid biosynthesis defects across genes including NFU1, BOLA3, IBA57, LIAS, and GLRX5 lead to convergent biochemical signatures characterized by impaired glycine cleavage, pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency, and elevated glycine and lactate levels in body fluids.

source.title: Differential diagnosis of lipoic acid synthesis defects
source.quote: Defects in the biosynthesis of LA have been reported to be associated with multiple and severe defects of the mitochondrial energy metabolism. In recent years, disease-causing mutations in genes encoding for proteins involved in LA metabolism have been reported: NFU1, BOLA3, IBA57, LIAS, GLRX5, LIPT1, ISCA2, and LIPT2.

evidence.text: Patients with biallelic GLRX5 mutations develop childhood-onset spastic paraparesis, non-ketotic hyperglycinemia, peripheral axonal neuropathy, and prominent upper cervical spinal cord signal abnormalities or leukoencephalopathy, mirroring findings seen in variant nonketotic hyperglycinemia and late-onset NFU1 mutations.

source.title: GLRX5-associated [Fe-S] cluster biogenesis disorder: further characterisation of the neurological phenotype and long-term outcome
source.quote: All patients (all females, age range 18-56 years) showed a complex neurological phenotype characterised by varying combinations of spastic paraparesis, length-dependent motor/sensory-motor axonal polyneuropathy, and psychiatric disturbances with variable intellectual disability. All had non-ketotic hyperglycinemia and a homozygous pathogenic c.151_153delAAG (p.K51del) change in GLRX5.

evidence.text: Variant nonketotic hyperglycinemia caused by mutations in GLRX5, BOLA3, and LIAS displays clinical overlap with NFU1 defects, featuring elevated serum and CSF glycine, deficient glycine cleavage activity, spastic paraplegia, spinal cord lesions, leukodystrophy, and reduced lipoylation of mitochondrial target proteins.

source.title: Variant non ketotic hyperglycinemia is caused by mutations in LIAS, BOLA3 and the novel gene GLRX5
source.quote: Patients with GLRX5-associated variant nonketotic hyperglycinemia had normal development with childhood-onset spastic paraplegia, spinal lesion, and optic atrophy... All patients had high serum and borderline elevated cerebrospinal fluid glycine and cerebrospinal fluid:plasma glycine ratio, and deficient glycine cleavage enzyme activity.

evidence.text: NFU1 mutations can present as a milder, slowly progressive spastic paraparesis phenotype with sensory-motor neuropathy, early white matter abnormalities, and high glycine concentration, closely mimicking variant NKH caused by defects in other Fe-S cluster biogenesis proteins.

source.title: New spastic paraplegia phenotype associated to mutation ...
source.quote: We report a new NFU1 mutated patient presenting with a milder phenotype characterized by a later onset, a slowly progressive spastic paraparesis with relapsing-remitting episodes, mild cognitive impairment and a long survival. The early white matter abnormalities observed on MRI was combined with a mixed sensory-motor neuropathy in the third decade. Our case clearly suggests the importance of considering NFU1 mutation in slowly evolving leukoencephalopathy with high glycine concentration.

numbers.metric: Patients described with milder NFU1 spastic paraparesis phenotype

new_directions.question_text: Can comprehensive quantitative profiling of mitochondrial lipoylated subcomplexes (PDH E2, OGDH E2, BCOADH E2) or acylcarnitine species distinguish NFU1 deficiency from GLRX5 or BOLA3 deficiency prior to sequencing?
new_directions.rationale: Different Fe-S cluster delivery proteins act at slightly distinct branch points in cofactor assembly, which may produce quantitative differences in the residual activity and lipoylation ratios of individual 2-oxoacid dehydrogenase complexes.

new_directions.question_text: Do spinal cord MRI imaging characteristics (such as dorsal column vs corticospinal tract restriction, contrast dynamics, or longitudinal lesion extent) systematically diverge between NFU1- and GLRX5-associated paraparesis?
new_directions.rationale: High-resolution neuroimaging comparisons across aggregated cohorts of variant NKH might reveal subtle anatomical predilections that standard routine clinical MRIs do not resolve.
